portsText: Per hybrid (2 on Hx2): 1 XLR female send input (pin 2 high, active balanced, mic/line switchable) and 1 XLR male receive output (pin 2 high, active balanced); telco line and phone-set RJ jacks (exact RJ type not stated); 1 DB9 remote per hybrid with ON/OFF control inputs and Ringing/ON-AIR status outputs (GPIO closures); optional plug-in AES3 module converting the XLRs to AES3 with sample-rate conversion; auto-ranging 90-265 VAC mains.
notes: NOT FOUND: dimensions, weight, rack units. Telos' Hx product page links a separate 'HX1 / HX2 Physical Dimensions' PDF that I could not locate or open; the Telos spec page (docs.telosalliance.com/docs/telos-specifications) and the Hx user manual PDF (404 on direct fetch) did not yield a physical section; dealer pages (BSW, PRG, Rentex, ManualsLib index) carry no size data. Tried: Telos product page, Telos docs spec page and .md copy, brochure PDF (404), QSG PDF (404), BSW, PRG, Rentex, ManualsLib. Search budget ran out before a dealer-spec search could be retried. Mix-minus ('clean feed' per hybrid) is a function of the device per Telos documentation but flags not extracted here. Rack height NOT confirmed (do not assume 1U).

portsText: 2-channel 1RU main station (up to 55 beltpacks or 10 speaker stations). Interfaces listed by Clear-Com: panel microphone input (electret), headset microphone input (dynamic), program line input, headset output, speaker output, partyline input and output, Stage Announce / balanced line out (balanced), IFB / hot-mic out (unbalanced). Connector types and pin counts (headset XLR 4 or 5 pin, etc.) NOT retrieved: the datasheet PDF returned 403.
notes: Axis order from source: H x W x D = 1.75 x 19 x 6.5 in = 44 x 483 x 165 mm; weight 6.1 lb (2.8 kg); 1RU. Search excerpt of the 2007 datasheet gives 6.06 lb (2.75 kg), consistent. Operating range 0-50 C. The RS-701 remote station (needed by the KB) was not researched.

portsText: Inputs: XLR 3-pin female, balanced, stereo L/R from the mixer output, plus an XLR 3-pin female balanced input for the telephone-fader feed (as reported by the Sonifex product page; counts of 2 plus 1 not cross-checked against the handbook). Output: 1 XLR 3-pin male, balanced L/R, to the TBU (hybrid or codec). Controls: output level, LF and full-band cancellation nulls, switchable 200 Hz-4 kHz band-pass. No headphone or mic feature listed. Powered from an external supply (not confirmed on the fetched page).
notes: Axis order from source: raw W x D x H = 28 x 10.8 x 4.3 cm. Net weight 1.1 kg (gross 1.5 kg boxed 36 x 20.5 x 6 cm). Adorama dealer lists 1.08 kg / 2.4 lb: rounding-level difference, manufacturer value used. Desktop box, not rack.

portsText: Analog in: 1 XLR-3-31 balanced (line or mic, phantom supported) + 1 RCA pair unbalanced; analog out: XLR-3-32 balanced + RCA pair; digital in: AES/EBU XLR-3-31 (110 ohm) + S/PDIF RCA; digital out: AES/EBU XLR-3-32 + S/PDIF RCA; phones 6.3 mm stereo jack; remote 2.5 mm TRS (RC-3F/RC-20); USB A-type (USB 2.0 HS); RS-232C DB9 female; parallel DB25 female (GPIO); Ethernet RJ45 100BASE-TX. Media: 2 SD slots (per KB) and CD-R/RW drive.
notes: Axis order from source: W x H x D = 482.6 x 45 x 300.5 mm; 1U rack; weight 3.2 kg. The sheet is the TEAC/TASCAM 'Product Spec Sheet SS-CDR250N' (Apr 2017). One reseller shows 2.9 kg and another ~3.2 kg; manufacturer value used. Power draw 22 W (search excerpt). Pinouts of the 14 ports not extracted beyond the XLR 1 GND / 2 HOT / 3 COLD.

portsText: 5P1000R (120 V US): 5 x NEMA 5-15R outlets (true sine, 1000 VA / 770 W), 5-15P input with 6 ft cord; RS-232 (RJ45) and USB (HID) as standard, 6 ft cables included; optional network card slot.
notes: Axis order from source: width 17.4 in x depth 20 in x height 1.7 in = 442 x 508 x 43 mm (1U); weight 32.5 lb = 14.7 kg (dealers 32.4 lb). One listing gives width 17.2 in (438 mm); one Elliott listing weight 45.63 appears to be shipping weight and is ignored. Values apply to the 5P1000R ONLY: the 5P1500R sibling and the 230 V (France) variants were NOT verified, so do not reuse these numbers for them. Colour not stated on the Eaton page.

portsText: Definition (cable family, not a box): connector A = Neutrik etherCON cable connector (NE8MX carrier fitted over a standard RJ45 plug; lockable, rugged shell); connector B = RJ45 plug or a second etherCON; straight-through Cat6/Cat6A, 8 conductors. Neutrik NE8MX accepts cable outer diameter 4.5-8 mm; the NE8MX6 Cat6 variant 7-9.5 mm (search excerpt of the NE8MX6 datasheet) and does not intermate with the Cat6 chassis connectors NE8FDY-C6.
notes: Typical lengths NOT found in a manufacturer source (no standard-length table obtained). Standards-level limit from a secondary source (Wikipedia, not graded): a Cat6 channel up to 100 m = 90 m permanent link plus 10 m of patch cords; Cat6 250 MHz, Cat6A 500 MHz; 10GBASE-T over Cat6 only to about 55 m. Cat6/Cat6A cable outer diameter not found. Argosy's sheet for the related NE8MX-1 variant gives 3.5-8 mm; check which variant is meant. Neutrik pages blocked other fetches (NE8MC variants returned 404).

portsText: Definition: connector A = Neutrik powerCON TRUE1 locking cable connector (NAC3FX-W, now succeeded by the TRUE1 TOP series, fully intermateable), 2 poles + PE, 16 A rms (USA 20 A), 250 V, IP65 when mated, screw terminals, cable outer diameter 6-12 mm, wire 1.0-2.5 mm2 (12 AWG), has breaking capacity (may be connected or disconnected under load). Connector B = IEC 60320 C13/C14 or CEE 7/7 type E plug at the far end: NOT sourced. Classic powerCON (NAC3FCA blue input / grey output, discontinued, successors NAC3FXXA-W-S 6-12 mm and -W-L 10-16 mm): 20 A 250 V, cable OD 6-15 mm, NO breaking capacity (must not be connected or disconnected under load).
notes: Important correction for the model: only TRUE1 can be mated under load; the older blue/grey powerCON cannot, per Neutrik's own sheets. Typical lengths for mains cords and IEC/Schuko/CEE 7/7 definitions were not obtained from a manufacturer or standard source: marked gap. Cable OD of the cord itself (H05VV-F 3G1.5 etc.) not sourced.

portsText: Definition: connector A and B = Neutrik speakON cable connectors, twist-lock. NL4FXX-W-S: 4 poles, cable OD 6-12 mm, wire 1.5-4 mm2 (17-11 AWG), up to 37 A rms (IEC 61984; UL 1977 35 A; CSA 24 A). NL4FXX-W-L: 4 poles, cable OD 10-16 mm, same ratings. NL2FX (discontinued, successor NL2FXX-W-S): 2 poles, 32 A rms, cable OD 6-10 mm, mates with 4-pole chassis connectors using +1/-1. NL8 (8-pole) not retrieved. Not for AC mains or for interrupting current.
notes: Typical cable lengths and loudspeaker-cable conductor gauge (2 x 2.5 mm2, 4 x 2.5 mm2) for a finished lead were not sourced. Contact numbering: NL4 pins 1+/1- and 2+/2-; NL2 uses 1+/1- (pole wiring not extracted from the sheets beyond the +1/-1 remark).

portsText: Definition: connector A and B = 1/4 in (6.35 mm) phone plugs. TRS = 3 contacts (tip, ring, sleeve; balanced mono or stereo); TS = 2 contacts (tip, sleeve; unbalanced mono). Neutrik NP3X (3-pole) and NP2X (2-pole): cable OD 4-7 mm, wire up to 1 mm2 (18 AWG), solder contacts, nickel shell, slim 14.5 mm shell width, more than 1000 mating cycles. 3.5 mm and 2.5 mm sizes per the secondary source (sleeve diameters 3.5 / 2.5 mm; 3.5 mm plug about 15 mm long). Adapter pairs for the KB (XLR-TRS, RCA-TS) not separately sourced.
notes: Mogami W2524 guitar cable (instrument cable family): overall diameter shown as 6.0 mm (0.236 in) in the Mogami catalogue (https://www.mogamicable.com/pdf/MogamiCatalog.pdf, table layout garbled in extraction, moderate confidence). Typical lengths (1, 3, 6 m) NOT found in a manufacturer source: gap. 3.5 mm Neutrik plug datasheet not fetched.

portsText: Definition: connector A = Neutrik NC3FXX (3-pole XLR female, nickel zinc-diecast shell, silver contacts); connector B = NC3MXX (3-pole XLR male); latch lock; rated 16 A per contact, cable OD 3.5-8.0 mm, wire max 2.5 mm2 (14 AWG), solder contacts, more than 1000 mating cycles. Balanced pinout (secondary source citing RS-297-A / AES14): pin 1 shield/ground, pin 2 hot (+), pin 3 cold (-). Mogami W2534 star-quad microphone cable: 4 conductors 24 AWG (OFC), overall diameter 6.0 mm, flexible PVC jacket, 10 colours.
notes: Typical lengths (1.5, 3, 6, 10 m) not found in a manufacturer table: gap. Dimensional standard IEC 61076-2-103 named by the secondary source (not fetched). Decision on cables as devices remains open (see plan).

portsText: Outputs: 1 balanced XLR output and 1 unbalanced RCA output; 1 XLR input for the built-in XLR cable test; Mini-B USB (5 pin) for wave-file mass storage and firmware; DC power-supply socket; powered by 3 x AA (LR6). Output impedance 200 ohm (MR2 column of the data table).
notes: Axis order from source: L x W x H = 152 x 81 x 43 mm including the protective shock jacket; mapped here as lying flat, w = 81, d = 152 (length), h = 43. Weight 310 g (11 oz) including batteries. The basic MR2 is 147 x 74 x 41 mm, 250 g (not this row). An older MR2 sheet found via RS lists 140 x 74 x 25 mm, 170 g for a previous-generation unit: ignore. Handbook is the NTi 'Minirator MR2/MR-PRO' manual hosted by Markertek; NTi spec PDFs returned 404.

portsText: Audio inputs: 1 XLR balanced (200 kohm, +48 V phantom switchable, auto-detects NTi ASD mics and MA220 preamp) and 1 RCA unbalanced (>30 kohm); built-in condenser mic for polarity/delay tests; outputs: built-in speaker, 3.5 mm mono headphone minijack; USB mini (data and charging); digital I/O interface for accessories (keypad, limit light, stack light); power: built-in 3.7 V Li-Po or 4 x AA or 9 VDC external; 1/4 in tripod mount plus wire stand on the rear.
notes: Axis order from source: L x W x H = 180 x 90 x 45 mm (7.1 x 3.5 x 1.8 in), weight 480 g (1 lb) including Li-Po. Mapped lying flat: w = 90, d = 180, h = 45. Values are for the XL2 analyzer body without the M2230/M4261 measurement microphone. The elimex copy is the NTi XL2 spec sheet; an NTi vibration-meter sheet repeats the same figures. Rear: mic/line input 4 (XLR female), Aux 1 line input (XLR female, Premium+), AES/Aux 2 (XLR female, Premium+), 2 line outputs (XLR male; Line Out 2 Premium+), 2 x RJ45 Ethernet 1000BaseT (AES67/RAVENNA, Premium+; also network), RJ45 ISDN S0 (option), Mini-B USB audio device, 4-pin male XLR for 12 V DC power, GPIO (2 inputs and 2 outputs), antenna connectors for the mobile options. Runs on 12 V DC or 6 x AA rechargeable batteries.
notes: Axis order from source: overall W x D x H = 212 x 236 x 102 mm. Weight: standard version less than 2.0 kg; Premium version with all options 2.1 kg, batteries NOT included (the feature table says less than 2.1 kg). The value 2.1 is the heaviest configuration. Numbers come from the user manual (datasheet grade); the separate datasheet PDF is a marketing brochure without physical specs.

portsText: Two-unit set. Send (pulse generator): 1/4 in output jack, XLR output, internal speaker. Receive (detector): 1 balanced 1/4 in input, 1 balanced XLR input. Tests female XLR pins 1/2/3 and tip/ring/sleeve of 1/4 in jacks (polarity and continuity). 9 V alkaline battery in each.
notes: Axis order from source: H x W x D. Receive unit 1.9 x 3.46 x 6.38 in = 48.26 x 87.88 x 162 mm; send unit 1.9 x 3.46 x 5.83 in = 48.26 x 87.88 x 148 mm (sizeMm above uses the larger receive unit). Weight 14.4 oz (408.2 g) per unit with battery; complete set shipped 33.6 oz (952.5 g). Some dealer listings show 3.375 x 1.812 x 6.25 in and 1.10 lb for an older/other package; manufacturer figures used. Colour not stated.

portsText: Inputs: 6 mic/line total, 3 on full-size XLR and 3 on TA3 (AES3 or AES42 available on XLR input 1); Aux 3.5 mm / 10-pin unbalanced 2-channel; Com Return TA3 and 3.5 mm; external slate mic TA5. Analog outputs: XLR L/R, TA3 X1/X2, 3.5 mm X3/X4 (6 total); AES3 digital outputs on XLR pairs (1-2 XLR-L, 3-4 XLR-R). Headphones 1/4 in and 3.5 mm, plus TA5 headset+mic. USB-C (file transfer) and USB-A host (keyboard, controller), 2 SD slots plus 256 GB internal SSD; power 10-18 V on locking TA4 (search excerpt of the spec sheet). Timecode connector type not confirmed.
notes: Axis order: the brochure gives 5.1 x 22 x 17 cm (H x W x D); dealers list 220 x 51 x 170 mm (W x H x D): the same box. Weight 2.75 lb / 1.25 kg unpackaged, without batteries (some dealers 1.3 kg). The brochure text was read via PDF text extraction; the spec-sheet PDF itself returned 403. Colour not stated.

portsText: 8 x XLR/TRS combo mic/line inputs (phantom +24/+48 V, +10 to +75 dB gain), dedicated MIC IN (Zoom capsule) and SLATE MIC, MAIN OUT 1/2 on TA3 (balanced), SUB OUT 1/2 on a 3.5 mm stereo mini (unbalanced), headphone out on a 1/4 in stereo jack, 2 x BNC timecode (in/out), Mini-B USB, DC in on a HIROSE HR10A-7R-4S 4-pin (9-18 V; AC adapter AD-19 12 V), 8 x AA battery compartment, 2 SD card slots (to 1 TB), 2.4 in LCD.
notes: Axis order from source: W x D x H = 7.0 x 5.5 x 2.1 in = 178.2 x 140.3 x 54.3 mm; weight 1200 g including batteries. Colour not stated. Retailer descriptions of the outputs vary slightly; the Zoom sheet was used.

portsText: Not applicable (passive furniture).

Standards-level facts (secondary source, not graded): panel width 482.6 mm (19 in) including ears; rail openings 450.85 mm apart (17.75 in), posts 15.88 mm wide; 1U = 44.45 mm (1.75 in); equipment panel height about 44.45 x n - 0.79 mm (about 43.66 mm for 1U); standards EIA-310-D/E, CEA-310-E, IEC 60297-3-100; no standard equipment depth (4-post cabinets are commonly 600, 800 or 1010 mm deep). Plain 6U-16U rack dimensions: derive height as n x 44.45 mm for the opening only.

portsText: Findings from the Mogami catalogue only. AES/EBU digital cable: 110 ohm (AES requirement), stated good to about 470 ft; bare-copper conductors; Mogami AES/EBU cable 3173 jacket appears as 7.8 mm (table layout garbled, moderate confidence). Gold AES patch cables in 3, 6, 12, 20 and 50 ft. 8-channel DB25 digital snakes in two formats: Tascam format (also used by Digidesign, Panasonic, RME and SSL) DB25-XLR in 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50 ft and DB25-DB25 in 5-25 ft; Yamaha format (also Apogee, Lynx, Mackie, Sony) DB25-XLR and DB25-DB25 in 5-25 ft; a Yamaha-to-Tascam crossover DB25-DB25 in 5-25 ft. BNC word clock / AES3id (75 ohm), TOSLINK ADAT and MADI cabling: NOT found.
notes: The DB25 pinouts remain unsourced: the catalogue states which brands use which format but not the pin assignments, so the earlier 'domain knowledge' pinouts still need AES/Tascam documentation. 75 ohm coax part 2964 is in the catalogue but its use (video vs digital) and OD were not confirmed from the garbled layout, so it is not quoted. TOSLINK/ADAT and MADI (BNC/SC optical) definitions not obtained from a manufacturer or standard.

portsText: FSII-BASE-II base station, 1RU: 4 x partyline A-D (XLR-3F), 4 x 4-wire (RJ45), program input (XLR-3F per datasheet text), stage announce output (XLR-3M), DB15 relay/GPIO, 2 x LAN (etherCON RJ45), 2 transceiver ports RJ45 plus fibre SFP, DECT sync RJ45, front headset jack (4-pin male or 5-pin female option), 12 V DC input (online manual also lists IEC C14), RF sync in/out. Beltpack FSII-BP19: NOT found.
notes: CONFLICT between two Clear-Com sources, so sizes left null. Datasheet FSII-BASE-II-5: 1.75 x 19.0 x 10.2 in (H x W x D) = 44 x 483 x 259 mm, 5.57 lb (2.5 kg). Online manual 'Specifications: Base Station' (FS-BASE-II-5 / FS-BASE-II): 44 x 442 x 250 mm (1.75 x 17.4 x 9.8 in), about 2.3 kg. Width may differ because of rack ears, but depth and weight differ too. Dealer sheets repeat the datasheet values. The older FSII-BASE (not II) is 1.75 x 19.0 x 12.5 in, 10.8 lb (dealer search excerpt) and must not be mixed in. The datasheet text lists program input as XLR-3F but its callout legend says XLR3M: a minor inconsistency. FSII-BP19 beltpack dimensions, weight and headset connector NOT found (search budget ran out).

portsText: Both DA-6400 and DA-6400dp: SMPTE LTC in/out (BNC), Word/Video in (BNC) and Thru/Out (BNC), Ethernet RJ45 (100BASE-TX / 1000BASE-T), RS-422 D-sub 9 female, parallel D-sub 15 female, USB 2.0 A-type, 1/4 in stereo phones jack, AC inlet (DA-6400dp has two power inlets for redundant power), and two slots for optional I/O cards (the audio connectors depend on the cards, e.g. DB25 or AES). 1U.
